comparison: Both evaluate the core in vivo findings (C5, C7, C8) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with in vitro data and tumor-specific effects, while peer reviewers affirm the 'notable reduction in tumor growth' and overall convincing demonstration. Complete agreement on primary efficacy claims.

Both address in vivo efficacy claims (C50, C51, C52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on bioluminescence imaging and immunofluorescence data showing tumor-specific effects, while peer reviewers affirm the 'notable reduction in tumor growth' and accept clarified experimental conditions. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate Sulfopin's effects on MYC pathway (C20, C21, C23, C25) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, Cut&Run, and western blot evidence with appropriate controls, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic findings and note authors 'nicely explained their rationale.' Complete agreement on MYC pathway modulation.

Both evaluate MYC expression-treatment sensitivity relationship (C35, C36, C37, C38) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes BLISS index calculations and statistical significance across eight DMG cultures, while peer reviewers specifically note authors 'nicely explained...the relationship between MYC expression and sensitivity.' Complete agreement.

Both evaluate transcriptomic findings on pathway suppression (C39, C40, C41, C42) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details RNA-seq, GSEA, western blot, and RT-qPCR validation, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse 'suppression of critical oncogenic pathways, particularly mTOR signaling.' Complete agreement on comprehensive transcriptomic analysis.

Both evaluate epigenetic mechanism findings (C44, C45, C46) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes single-molecule imaging validation of western blot results, while peer reviewers accept the epigenetic data and note clarified experimental conditions. Peer review also includes C47-C48 (histone modifications) which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Both evaluate histone modification changes (C47, C48) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on Cut&Run data showing coordinated H3K27ac and H3K27me3 changes, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the broader epigenetic mechanism without specific critique. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate Sulfopin monotherapy effects and H3-K27M-dependent sensitivity (C26, C27, C28) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes isogenic knockout controls strengthening conclusions, while peer reviewers accept these supporting findings without question. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate correlative analyses linking MYC expression to treatment response (C29, C30, C31) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the paradox of low PIN1 expression in responsive tumors but accepts the analysis, while peer reviewers affirm the relationship between MYC expression and sensitivity. OpenEval also addresses C32-C33 and C61; peer review includes C32-C33 in their acceptance.

Both evaluate cell cycle correlations (C32, C33) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details statistically significant correlations across eight DMG cultures, while peer reviewers accept these correlations as part of the broader MYC expression-sensitivity relationship. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate Vorinostat's effects on enhancer activity (C49) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details Cut&Run data and pathway enrichment analysis linking enhancer regions to target genes, while peer reviewers accept this mechanistic detail without question. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate the negative survival result (C62) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval interprets rapid deterioration as reflecting tumor aggressiveness rather than toxicity, while peer reviewers acknowledge this limitation without challenge and accept it as honest reporting. Complete agreement on the finding and its interpretation.

Both address biomarker proposals (C43, C74, C75). OpenEval evaluates C43 and C75 as SUPPORTED with comprehensive transcriptomic validation, while peer reviewers accept these translational implications as potential rather than validated biomarkers. Complete agreement on the supporting evidence.

Both address C74 (MYC expression as biomarker). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with extensive cell viability data and BLISS index calculations, while peer reviewers accept this biomarker proposal without challenge. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate foundational background claims (C1-C4, C9-C13) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes extensive citations to published literature establishing field knowledge, while peer reviewers accept the background and rationale, stating the work 'contributes to the study of H3-K27M mutated pediatric gliomas.' Complete agreement on foundational context.

Both evaluate clinical rationale claims (C14, C15, C53-C55) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multiple citations to published studies and clinical trials, while peer reviewers accept the background establishing scientific premise. Complete agreement on clinical context.

Both evaluate MYC biology background claims (C16, C17, C56-C59) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes established knowledge about MYC in cancer biology, while peer reviewers accept this foundational context without challenge. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate Sulfopin background claims (C6, C18, C19, C60) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes citation to Dubiella et al., 2021 and accurate representation of prior work, while peer reviewers accept this background as part of the scientific premise. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate mTOR pathway background claims (C63-C66) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes citations to published literature providing context for observed pathway downregulation, while peer reviewers accept this background without challenge. Complete agreement.

Both address viral mimicry and interferon response background (C67-C71). OpenEval evaluates these as SUPPORTED but notes C76 and C80 are UNCERTAIN speculative inferences, while peer reviewers accept the background literature without distinguishing between established knowledge and speculative mechanisms. Partial agreement on background, but OpenEval identifies speculative elements.

OpenEval evaluates C34 (H3K27me3 reduction at CGIs) as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative and contradicts known requirements for residual H3K27me3. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this mechanistic detail was not specifically addressed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates C78-C79 (specific MYC-mTOR interaction mechanism) as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanism is speculative and not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted the broader mTOR pathway findings but did not specifically evaluate this mechanistic inference.

OpenEval addresses C61 (PIN1 expression paradox) as part of R7 evaluation (SUPPORTED but paradox noted), while peer reviewers include C61 in their general acceptance of background claims (R12). OpenEval identifies an unresolved paradox that peer reviewers did not specifically address.

OpenEval evaluates C77 (interpretation of rapid deterioration) as SUPPORTED, noting it reflects tumor aggressiveness rather than toxicity. While peer reviewers accepted C62 (the negative survival result), they did not specifically evaluate this interpretive claim C77 separately.
